ui-backdrop: The floor of every interactive scene: put it on the bottom track for the whole timeline and every ui-* control reads well on it (its glows drift on the session clock, so a scene waiting for input still breathes). Pitfall: it is opaque, so under footage or a photo leave it out or put the picture above it. Works: style "grid", glow 0.5 for a game; style "plain", vignette 0.3 for a calm quiz; a second scene with its own colorA so a transition reads as a new place. Pairs with all ui-* controls and transitions.
ui-button: The one thing to do next. A primary button at the bottom of a vertical scene (width 100 in a safe box 0.9 wide, size 12: a thumb-sized target), a secondary and a ghost under it with delay 0.08 and 0.16. Pitfall: keep outDur 0 when the scene holds for input (the playhead waits on the scene's last frame, so an exit would leave it half faded); a label that cannot fit its box at the 2.6 % floor throws instead of shrinking. Works: { "label": "Start", "icon": "arrow-right", "hotkey": "Enter" }; disabled bound to a boolean while a dialog is open. Pair with ui-tx-iris (the next scene opens from the tap on it) and ui-dialog.
ui-card: Answers of a quiz, a picker, a memory game. Bind every card of a set to one variable ("choice": { "$var": "pick" }) and set it from each card's select with "$value"; give them all the same answer and bind reveal to a boolean the clip sets after a pick. Pitfall: value defaults to the title (two cards with one title pick together), and reveal locks the whole set. Works: a 2 x 2 grid in a vertical frame, each 0.46 x 0.19 of the safe area, badges A to D, hotkeys 1 to 4, delay i x 0.07; icon cards (icon + title + detail) for a difficulty picker in a wide frame. Pair with ui-toast (success / error after the reveal), ui-score and ui-progress dots.
ui-menu: Main menus, settings lists, level select: one region per option (id = its index), number keys and Tab + Enter. For a highlight that follows taps, set emit "index", bind highlight to a number variable and wire { "on": "menu.select", "do": { "set": { "row": "$value" } } }; ArrowDown / ArrowUp wires with add and wrap move it from the keyboard. Pitfall: with emit "value" the event carries the option's value (or label), which cannot drive highlight; locked options show a lock and take no taps. Works: a title, 4 or 5 options with icons, rowSize 10.5 in a safe box 0.92 x 0.5. Pair with ui-tx-push (forward into the picked scene, back with direction right) and ui-dialog for a destructive option.
ui-toggle: Settings rows (sound, vibration, hints). The whole row is the target and change carries the new boolean: { "set": { "sound": "$value" } } (or { "toggle": "sound" }). Pitfall: without a bound `on` it emits but never moves. Works: three rows in safe boxes 0.92 x 0.11, 0.125 apart, a detail line on the ones that need it, delay 0.06 apart; plate false over a plain backdrop in a wide frame. Pair with ui-slider in the same settings scene and a ghost ui-button "Done" to leave it.
ui-slider: Volume, speed, difficulty, a guess on a scale. The track is a range region: dragging and the arrow keys (after Tab) both emit change with the value snapped to step. Pitfall: bind value, or the thumb stays where it was; display "auto" shows a percentage for a 0 to 1 range with no prefix, suffix or decimals, the value otherwise. Works: { "label": "Speed", "min": 0.5, "max": 2, "step": 0.25, "decimals": 2, "suffix": "×" } (ticks show for 2 to 12 steps). Pair with ui-toggle in a settings scene; send it pulse to point at it in a tutorial.
ui-progress: Where the viewer is: dots for "question 3 of 5", a bar for a timer or a level, a ring for a share of a goal. Bind value (and max): it glides to each new value, a reached dot pops, and it fills in from zero when it appears. Pitfall: dots count round(max) steps (2 to 12), so use the bar for fractions; an item spanning several scenes fills in only once. Works: style "dots", max 5, label "Question" in a safe box 0.9 x 0.08 at the top; a bar with showValue "none" and color the second accent as a timer. Pair with ui-score in the opposite corner and ui-card answers; send it pulse after a right answer.
ui-score: Scores, lives, coins and countdowns in a HUD. Bind value and add to the variable from the wires: the number ticks, pops, flashes (red on a loss) and floats the difference. Pitfall: the pop and the floating "+10" reach outside the item's box, so leave room around it; the stack style uses the display face (Anton), whose digits are not tabular, so place it centred. Works: a pill { "label": "Score", "icon": "star" } top right (safe 0.8, 0.07, 0.38 x 0.1), a plain { "icon": "heart", "color": "#ff5c8a" } for lives top left, a stack with size 14 on a results screen. Pair with ui-progress and ui-toast.
ui-dialog: Confirmations and modal news (leave the game? level complete): Enter confirms, Escape cancels, a tap on the scrim cancels (or is swallowed with scrimTap "block"), and nothing under it takes a tap. Pitfall: an item shown with `when` keeps its scene's time, so send it open as it appears to replay the entrance, or bind open and leave `when` out (then it also animates out); give it the whole frame as its box, on the top track. Works: tone "danger" with icon "trash-2" for a destructive choice; one button (cancel "") with tone "success" and icon "trophy" for good news. Pair with disabled bound to the same variable on the controls under it, and ui-toast after a confirm.
ui-hotspot: Exploring a picture or a held frame of footage: a pulsing marker per point of interest that opens its own scene or a toast, ticked once visited (bind visited). Pitfall: phones have no hover, so use labelOn "always" there (focus also shows the label); give it the picture item's transform and fit, and the picture's pixel size as space. Works: size 7 with icon "plus" (it turns a quarter on hover), or mark "1", "2", "3" for an order; ping it after a while as a hint. Pair with ui-tx-zoom (dive into the spot from the tap), ui-toast for a one-line fact and ui-progress ("found 2 of 5").
ui-toast: Feedback that comes and goes: send it success, error or show with the text as the value from any wire (show takes a tone prefix: "ok: …", "error: …", "info: …", "warn: …"). Pitfall: it draws nothing until an event arrives (blank in stills and the thumbnail) unless text is set; a message longer than two lines at the floor throws, so keep it short. Works: one toast item for the whole timeline, edge "top", hold 1.8, success "Correct, +10" and "error: Not quite" from the answer wires; text with hold 0 for a status line in a video. Pair with ui-card reveals, ui-score and ui-button presses.
ui-tx-push: Moving forward and back between app-like screens: interactive.transition (direction left) for forward, a go action with direction "right" on back wires. Pitfall: it moves the whole frame, so scenes with the same backdrop read as content sliding, different backdrops as a new screen; keep it under 0.6 s or it feels slow on a phone. Works: duration 0.45 to 0.5, parallax 0.3, dim 0.45, depth 0.04. Pair with ui-menu (each option pushes to its scene) and a ghost ui-button "Back".
ui-tx-iris: Opening the next scene from what was tapped: the pressed button seems to swell into the next screen, edged by a glowing ring in the theme's accent. Pitfall: after a key or a timer the pointer is the last one (or none), so set origin "center" or a point for those wires; in a video it always opens from x, y. Works: duration 0.6 to 0.7 on the go action of a Play button low in the frame. Pair with ui-button and ui-card (pick a card, open its scene).
ui-tx-zoom: Diving into a detail and pulling back out: mode "in" towards the tap on a hotspot or a card, mode "out" on the way back. Pitfall: the middle is a double exposure of both scenes, so keep it short (0.5 to 0.6 s) and the two layouts different. Works: amount 0.6 with streaks for a game, streaks off for a calm explainer. Pair with ui-hotspot (dive into the spot) and ui-tx-push for sideways moves.
